title: Cosmic Latte: The Average Color of the Universe
explanation:
# The Universe's True Color

When astronomers averaged the light from 200,000 galaxies, they discovered that if you could somehow blend all the starlight in the night sky together, the universe would appear as a warm, creamy beige—a shade so specific it has the computer code #FFF8E7 and earned the playful name "cosmic latte." Over the past 10 billion years, this cosmic color has shifted from blue toward red, revealing that older, redder stars are becoming increasingly dominant as galaxies age.
